name: agent-fs-write-operations
body:
Code-writer implementer agents delete, move, and copy files inside the surface they own, so a plan task with a deletes / renames / moves verb is implementable.

The capability lives in a suite of filesystem tools — apg_rm, apg_mv, apg_cp — installed by apg init as opencode 2.x plugins, which SELF-ENFORCE their scope: each tool keeps its operation inside the acting agent's granted globs under the opencode 2.x `permissions` model, refuses any path outside them, and resolves the granted globs and the candidate in one consistent frame. The agent's effective `edit`-action scope is the ordered combination of the lower-priority configuration, the global rules, and the agent's own rules last, with the last matching rule winning; opencode resolves a path that matches zero rules to `ask`, while the tool applies its OWN fail-closed default and refuses a zero-match path (deny-by-default). The fs scope tracks that `edit` scope: the fs tools touch zero path the agent's `edit` rules deny (see `requirements.note.fs-scope-deny-mirror`). The tool-level grant (deny-by-default) is the callability gate alone; per-path scoping lives inside the tool. For a code-writer the granted globs are WORKTREE-ONLY — apg/.worktrees/*/<glob> — the repo-root path is outside them (see `requirements.requirement.code-writer-worktree-only-writes`): opencode resolves path-scoped globs against the session workspace root (the main checkout), so the worktree form reaches the worktree, while a root grant reaches main. This is a scoped capability with zero blanket grant: a path outside the agent's granted globs (or revoked by a later deny rule) is refused, a path resolving into the main checkout is refused, and an operation is confined to the project/worktree boundary.

The way a tool learns the acting agent's identity and effective `permissions` rules under opencode 2.x is the accepted open item of `requirements.constraint.agent-fs-per-path-permission`, verified by unit/int tests against a faked V2 tool context. An unresolvable acting agent refuses every path (fail-closed).

Scope: rm + mv + cp alone. Product source (opencode-suite/** tool files, opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts, opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md) plus the binary's install registry. External to the repo's own .opencode/agents/**. Plain filesystem operations alone — zero git rm/git mv — and zero change to the binary's node/edge mutation surface.

Acceptance criteria:
- apg init installs the three tools as opencode 2.x plugins under `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`; rust.apg.install's plugin registry carries one entry per tool.
- A generated implementer agent's `permissions` array grants apg_rm/apg_mv/apg_cp scoped to exactly its owned path globs under apg/.worktrees/*/ (worktree-only; zero repo-root variant); the tool self-enforces that scope per path.
- An fs-op whose source path (and, for mv/cp, destination path) is matched by a grant with zero later deny override succeeds; a path outside the granted globs, or revoked by a later deny rule, is refused.
- The fs tools honour deny rules: a deny rule that is the LAST matching rule refuses the operation, mirroring the agent's `edit` scope. A pure unit test over fsScopeDecision pins the deny/order semantics; the opt-in boundary e2e pins the acting-agent scope read (allow AND deny read as ordered rules).
- An fs-op whose path escapes the project/worktree boundary, or resolves into the main checkout, is refused.
- An unresolvable acting agent refuses every path (fail-closed).
- The install-assertion e2e (rust.main_e2e.e2e.suite_installs_node_edge_project_tools_and_retires_spec_invariant) asserts the three tools are embedded and installed under `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`.
